newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia propels lively Helsinki to 2.5 pct rise.
newsitem.headline: Nokia propels lively Helsinki to 2.5 pct rise.

text.p: Shares ended higher in massive volume on Tuesday with the HEX index tacking on more than two percent after Nokia powered up on its report of sharply higher first-quarter earnings, brokers said.

The general HEX index rose 2.51 percent to 2,930.53 points and volume was a very lively 1.26 billion markka, 71 percent of which was in Nokia. The FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark rose 2.33 percent to 1,019 points.
"This has been Nokia's day," one broker said.

Nokia added 20.90 markka, or more than six percent, to close at 321.90 markka. Both Nokia shares were traded heavily, with the combined volume rising above 900 million markka, to account for more than 70 percent of total bourse turnover.
A higher open from U.S. stocks and bonds, and for Nokia on Wall St, bolstered sentiment late in the session, brokers said.

"This now looks very bullish. If U.S. bonds stay up there and stocks follow them, then tomorrow could be quite a day," one broker said as the U.S. markets opened higher with help from Q1 employment cost data.
Forestries, banks and metal shares added width to the rise, with the sub-indices up 1.07 percent, 4.06 percent and 0.98 percent respectively.
Steel group Rautaruukki added 2.70 to end at 46.50 in heavy 65 million markka volume after it yesterday set its share offering price at 42.00 markka per share.
As the market closed, Rautaruukki said it would up its public offering from four million shares to 7.4 million.
Insurer Pohjola ended 1.00 markka higher at 148.00, helped by news that it was pursuing its plans to absorb Suomi insurance by buying Suomi's Salama shares, brokers said.
The largest banking group Merita closed 0.80 markka higher at 17.20 after touching 17.20 in fairly lively trade, helped by the downward shift in interest rates late in the session, brokers said.
